title: Deciphering the role of chemical signals in inflammation with open microfluidic functional assays
text:
Molecular communication across cell types is central to life—communication between cell types in a human
organ is critical to normal function, and microbe-host or microbe-microbe communication drives microbial
ecosystems. This proposal will study signaling between human immune cells and fibroblasts and signaling
between microbes relevant for human health (e.g., commensal and pathogenic bacteria and fungi). We will
develop a suite of microfluidic tools to broaden the scope of mechanistic questions that can be addressed,
ultimately enabling the development of therapies to target dysfunctional signaling and inflammation in human
disease.

title: Association of Phenotypes and Genotype with Treatment Response in Psoriatic Arthritis
text:
Despite an increasing number of therapeutic options for psoriatic arthritis (PsA), a chronic progressive
inflammatory disease of the skin and musculoskeletal system affecting over half a million Americans, less than
a third of patients respond to therapy. This is, in part, because PsA is studied and managed as if it were a single
disease. In this proposal, we will use two unique real-world PsA cohorts to better understand clinical and genetic
heterogeneity in PsA and to identify those who are more likely or less likely to respond to therapy.

title: Mechanisms of Assembly and Functional Regulation in Non-canonical Biomolecular Condensates
text:
Proteins-only biomolecular condensates are a crucial part of normal cellular processes and their mis-regulation
is at the heart of various pathologies. Unfortunately, current understanding on what sequence motifs promote
the assembly of such condensates and the biophysical principles that regulate their composition and dynamics
has been limited. Discoveries from this work will provide a framework in fundamental understanding of these
condensates and bring new opportunities to prevent, diagnose, and treat condensate-driven diseases.

title: Structure-based discovery and development of next-generation sCD4 immunotherapeutics for HIV
text:
HIV remains a major public health challenge because existing therapies suppress viral replication
but do not eliminate infected cells or viral reservoirs. This project seeks to develop a new class of
soluble CD4 (single D1 domain)-based bifunctional immunotherapies that not only block HIV
infection with broad potency but also harness the immune system to eliminate HIV-infected cells.
Successful completion of this work could enable durable, ART-free HIV remission and directly
supports NIH and HHS priorities in advancing innovative treatments for HIV/AIDS.

title: An Engineered Bioprinting Platform to Study Neural Migration in Assembloids
text:
Human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived neural assembloids represent a powerful tool to study
neural interactions across multiple brain regions; unfortunately, current assembloid generation protocols
commonly yield randomly oriented, heterogeneous structures with limited spatial control, which significantly limits
their application in functional studies. We propose to develop a novel, non-destructive 3D-bioprinting technology
to pattern reproducible, precise, and spatially-relevant, assembloid structures as in vitro models for studying
interneuron migration in neurodevelopment and its disorders. The success of our work will establish a
transformational technology that yields robust and reproducible assembloids for in vitro functional investigations
into human brain development and diseases, with proof of concept studies targeting autism spectrum disorder.

title: Transcriptional overload: unlocking a new anti-cancer paradigm by targeting DDX19A
text:
This proposal is relevant to public health as it identifies the mechanism of action of the RNA helicase DDX19A,
a regulator of transcription in the bone malignancy Ewing sarcoma. This research will also lead to the
development of first-in-class small molecule inhibitors of DDX19A which will serve as future therapeutics in this
aggressive disease. Thus, since this work addresses the critical need to determine novel approaches to target
cancer-driving transcription factors, the proposed research is also relevant to the NCI mission of advancing
fundamental knowledge to enhance health and reduce illness and disability from cancer.

title: TopoROP: Multi-View Topology-Integrated Analytics for Diagnosis of Retinopathy of Prematurity
text:
TOPOROP: MULTI-VIEW TOPOLOGY-INTEGRATED ANALYTICS FOR DIAGNOSIS OF RETINOPATHY OF
PREMATURITY
RELEVANCE. With increasing survival of premature infants, largely due to improved perinatal and neonatal care, Retinopa-
thy of Prematurity (ROP) is the leading cause of preventable childhood blindness globally, resulting in significant societal
costs from lost productivity. We introduce a novel multi-view framework that models retinal vascular topology with deep
learning at the network level to derive interpretable biomarkers for comprehensive quantification of ROP disease progression
to secure optimal treatment outcomes. By enabling more efficient, accurate and objective screening for telemedicine, this
topology-integrated model will decrease the prevalence of preventable vision loss in both childhood and adulthood to combat
the latest epidemiological phase of ROP.

title: Non-coding RNA structure change in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
text:
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) affects between 5 and 7% percent of the adult US population.
Most mutations associated with COPD change regions of the genome that do not code for protein but are
transcribed into RNA. By combining RNA sequencing analysis of lungs from COPD patients with novel RNA
structure probing technologies to identify functional RNA structures in COPD associated genes, we will illuminate
new causative features of COPD and, over longer periods, inspire new RNA-based therapeutic strategies.

title: Motion Adaptive Neural Interfaces for Brain-Body Communication
text:
This project will create soft, motion-adaptive hydrogel microelectrodes that can stably record neural activity from
the spinal cord and internal organs while animals move and breathe normally. These tools will help scientists
understand how the brain communicates with the body through spinal and autonomic circuits and may guide
new treatments for spinal cord injury, autonomic dysfunction, and gut-brain axis disorders.

title: Impact of Shiftwork on Metabolic Flexibility and Skeletal Muscle Clocks
text:
Shiftwork is now recognized as a risk factor for type 2 diabetes, yet the mechanisms underlying these
associations are poorly understood. Herein, we will test the hypothesis that real-world nightshift work impairs
whole-body metabolic flexibility across the 24h day-night cycle, and that this will be associated with disrupted
skeletal muscle clocks. To test this hypothesis, we will conduct rigorously controlled in-patient studies to assess
and compare whole-body metabolic flexibility using innovative 24h metabolic chamber protocols, as well as
skeletal muscle clock function by comparing diurnal shifts in skeletal muscle clock genes, in dayshift versus
nightshift workers.

title: Mount Sinai Alzheimer's Disease Research Center
text: The Mount Sinai Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center is dedicated to using our strengths in genetics and genomics to serve our cohort at risk for ADRD by studying the relationship between the polygenic risk scores (PRS), fluid and imaging biomarkers, cognitive phenotype, and neuropathological profiles to identify pathways of vulnerability or resistance to disease to improve diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of ADRD.

title: A computational framework for quality assessment and curation of models at scale
text:
Although modeling is an important component of a research pipeline in biology, there is no systematic or
standardized approach for quality assessment and annotation of models, thus reducing their trustworthiness and
reuse potential. Our goal is to standardize and fully automate the iterative process of assembly, documentation,
and assessment of models of cell signaling, and as such, maximize the model reuse potential and their long-
term value, while minimizing the risk for models to become obsolete. The objective of this proposal is to develop
a computational framework that allows researchers to automatically verify, validate, annotate, modify, and update
their models using open access information in published literature and databases.

title: The chemical language of human gut bacteria in healthy aging
text:
This research is relevant to public health because elucidating how microbiome-derived bioactive molecules
regulate host aging can reveal molecular targets to mitigate age-related decline and promote healthy aging. It
directly supports the NIH mission to advance fundamental knowledge that improves health and reduces the
burden of age-associated disease.

title: Placental and breastmilk microRNAs in relation to early-life growth and metabolism
text:
Gestational and early childhood exposures, including maternal metabolic status and breastfeeding, are
increasingly recognized as critical in the development of childhood and life-long obesity. The proposed
research seeks to comprehensively assess the impact of maternal metabolic status on early childhood growth
and metabolism, through the gene regulatory dynamics of placental and breastmilk microRNAs. This research
has the potential to advance our understanding of the contribution of microRNAs and early-life exposures on
growth and metabolism, and to more broadly contribute the Developmental Origins of Health and Disease.

title: Application of precision medicine to phototherapy: a stepped care approach to consolidate sleep and slow cognitive decline in older adults
text:
Consolidated sleep is crucial for older individuals' cognition, health, and well-being, but the fragmentation of
sleep and wake increases with age. This study will investigate underlying mechanisms contributing to sleep-
wake fragmentation and explore the utility of a novel intervention, afternoon phototherapy, to reduce the
consequences of sleep-wake fragmentation, including ameliorated cognition. Results from this project may lead
to an inexpensive or free scalable intervention with the potential to ameliorate cognitive decline and other
concomitants of fragmented sleep, delay institutionalization, and improve the quality of life in older individuals.

title: Center Core Grant for Vision Research
text:
(Overall)
The renewal of this Vision Research Core Grant is to request continuing funds by 22 vision scientists (holding
15 core-eligible NEI R01 grants) to provide crucially needed expertise and instrumentation to enable and
enhance NEI-R01 funded vision research at the James and Jean Vision Discovery Institute (VDI) with members
from Augusta University, and UGA Clinical and Experimental Therapeutics group in Augusta. We have organized
the services and shared instrumentation into three modules: 1) Functional Vision Assessment; 2) Histology and
Imaging; and 3) Bioinformatics and Biostatistics Support, led by NEI-R01 funded VDI researchers to enhance
the capability of vision scientists at VDI performing cutting-edge research/discovery of blindness and visual
disorders.

title: Investigating the impact of chromosomal instability on prostate cancer aggressiveness
text:
Advanced lethal prostate cancer (PC) exhibits high chromosomal instability (CIN), yet the role of CIN in PC
remains poorly understood. This proposal will investigate how CIN shapes transcriptional reprogramming and
gene bookmarking, identify new proteins and mechanisms of CIN adaptation, and study CIN impact on the
immune cell microenvironment in advanced PC. Combining epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, high-
resolution microscopy, and genetics in in vitro and in vivo models our studies will help define novel PC
vulnerabilities arising with CIN and uncover new targetable mechanism that may improve PC patients outcomes.

title: Mechanisms Underlying the HIV-HSV-2 Syndemic
text:
Herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) is one of the most significant factors fueling the global HIV
epidemic and coinfection is associated with higher HIV plasma viral loads and increased rates
of HIV transmission. The goal of this application is to identify the mechanisms by defining the
transcriptional responses to HSV-2 in HIV-infected individuals using primary cells and genital
skin biopsies obtained during HSV-2 recurrences and to determine how these responses
promote HIV replication. The results obtained will have broad implications and accelerate the
development of strategies for HIV eradication.

title: Computational Population Genetics
text:
In this MIRA proposal we seek to continue our work at developing computational methods for
population genetic inference from whole genome data. We propose three areas of interest: 1) spatial
population genetics, 2) the population genetics of adaptation, and 3) development of community
library aimed at improving rigor and reproducibility in the field. We will produce multiple tools and
resources that will usher in the next generation of inference for the incredibly rich genomic data
currently under collection.

title: Basal airway epithelial cell dysfunction in lung cancer development
text:
Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC), the second most common subtype of lung cancer, continues to have
limited treatment options and cause significant mortality. The series of bronchial premalignant lesions (PMLs)
that precede LUSC may serve as a target for early targeted chemoprevention strategies. We propose to use
in-vitro and in-vivo models to understand the changes in the transcriptome and chromatin states during the
early development of LUSC to identify novel targets for LUSC chemoprevention and assess the efficacy of a
small molecule inhibitor in intercepting bronchial PML progression.
